scope: Metric lifting and physical validation of the named active flower-stem track
summary: One 17-sample SAM2 stem track was lifted through DA3 into a 12-node world-frame centerline, but the result was correctly rejected because temporal segment-length CV reached 1.857 against the immutable 0.12 gate.
evidence: All 17 requested source frames were extracted without errors and nominal node visibility was 100 percent.
Centerline extraction ran in 0.3082 seconds at 55.1656 stem-frames per second.
The persistent-ID, confidence, visibility, and metric-geometry gates pass while temporal segment-length rigidity fails with maximum CV 1.857228434776532.
lessons: A per-frame mask skeleton can cross foreground/background depth discontinuities and cannot preserve a thin stem's material arc length.
A high visible-pixel fraction is not evidence of a physically consistent 3-D centerline.
limitations: Only one sparse active-stem mask exists for source frames 272 through 320; the other manipulated stems and long occlusions are unobserved.
The rejected estimate cannot be used for real contact-force inversion.
next_actions: Replace independent skeleton lifting with V-DPM or SpaTracker point identities and jointly optimize an occlusion-aware rooted rod while keeping the 0.12 rigidity threshold fixed.
